basis: Disease of cerebral vessels and the brain tissue supplied by them.
Congenital absence of both upper limbs.
Radiation-induced lung inflammation; radiation injury does not itself establish an infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Microcephaly, structural brain abnormalities, severe developmental impairment and seizures define the disorder.
Degeneration of the retinal macula.
Methylmercury-induced encephalopathy and sensory pathway injury; additional organ damage is not established at the required frequency.
Neurodevelopmental regression defines Rett; muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79% and scoliosis in ~52%. Abnormal breathing reflects neural control, not lung damage.
Congenital obliteration of pulmonary veins; these vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
Short ribs, narrow thorax and polydactyly define the skeletal disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia is common across severe forms, exceeding ~30% overall.
LIG1 immunodeficiency; multicystic kidney dysplasia in 2/5 (40%). Macrocytosis alone does not establish blood dysfunction; recurrent infections do not prove lasting lung injury.
Encephalitis with infectious/postinfectious or autoimmune mechanisms; eye movement abnormalities reflect CNS injury rather than ocular disease.
Neuronal migration disorder with heterotopia, developmental impairment and seizures; isolated extracerebral findings do not establish common organ damage.
Recurrent intra-articular bleeding causes joint destruction; underlying hemophilia is a separately diagnosed coagulation disorder.
Congenital ventricular and atrioventricular valve malformation.
Congenital malposition of the urethral opening; the urethra is explicitly included in the renal axis.
Chronic destructive bronchiolar inflammation with obstruction and bronchiectasis; associated sinus disease belongs to the same axis.
Partial displacement of the ocular lens.
Photosensitive brittle-hair disorder, often with ichthyosis; neurodevelopmental impairment affects most (~70-85%). DNA repair deficiency alone does not establish metabolic organ disease.
Tumour arises from odontogenic epithelium; the solid/multicystic form occupies and destroys jaw bone in most cases.
Defined by paraneoplastic renal dysfunction; immune, endocrine and skeletal features are subtype-dependent.
Acute, usually infectious inflammation of the larynx and pharynx, both within the pulmonary axis.
Inherited skeletal disease defined by reduced bone density and fragility fractures; no separate endocrine dysfunction is established.
Defective neuronal norepinephrine reuptake causes autonomic dysfunction and defining orthostatic tachycardia; neurotransmitter excess is not endocrine disease.
Congenital presence of additional kidneys.
Prenatal methylmercury causes brain injury; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Visual impairment (80-99%) commonly reflects cerebral injury, without established direct eye damage.
